Daily US-Israel-Iran War Brief:
14th Aug 2026:

- We will be posting daily war updates on the ongoing war in Middle East
- ⁠Follow us for daily Brief

● US officials reported that they have received several warnings from Israel over the past year indicating that Iran intended to assassinate President Donald Trump, though US intelligence agencies could not independently verify these claims.

● US Vice President JD Vance stated that Washington is utilizing diplomatic, military, and economic tools "very selectively, very strategically" to pressure Iran, aiming to prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and to ensure the stability of global energy prices.

● US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that the US military could maintain its naval blockade of Iran "indefinitely" by rotating ships in and out of the region. Concurrently, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced plans to apply measures "never been seen" on Iran, focusing on unprecedented economic isolation and a continued blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

● US Central Command (CENTCOM) reported that as of August 12, US forces enforcing the blockade had redirected 59 commercial vessels linked to the Iranian regime, disabled three, and boarded two for inspection. Tanker-tracking companies indicated that Iran's oil exports have completely halted since the naval blockade began.

● President Donald Trump described the US naval blockade as a "steel wall," asserting that the US has full control of the Strait of Hormuz. In response, the IRGC's Persian Gulf Waterway Management Authority claimed the strait remains closed and will not reopen until Iran's conditions are accepted.

● The United Arab Emirates blamed Iran for hostile attacks on two vessels affiliated with the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) as they transited the Strait of Hormuz, noting there were no injuries reported.

● Israel's Defense Minister clarified that Israeli forces will not withdraw from southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is completely disarmed, qualifying earlier remarks about an indefinite occupation that had drawn US criticism.

● President Trump directed future US Navy aircraft carriers to abandon advanced launch systems in favor of older, proven steam catapult technologies to address long-term shipbuilding and repair issues highlighted during the conflict.

END OF THE BRIEF
